scope: Independent H05/H07 archived-source field audit, not full hardware package acceptance

status_definitions.source_table_claim_supported: Positive archived content check, restricted to cited scope; not just pointer presence
status_definitions.unresolved: Any status prefixed unresolved requires further evidence or preserved unknown
status_definitions.instruction_type_supported_peak_mapping_: Instruction legality proved; advertised-rate mapping remains unaccepted

F01.title: Derived GB200 dense peaks are recorded without formulas
F01.detail: GB200 page footnote 2 explicitly halves sparse rates. Dense FP8, FP6, BF16, FP16, TF32 and INT8 rows have derivation=null and reported contains the derived number rather than the sparse original.

F02.title: Original reported units lost during normalization
F02.detail: Rubin, GB200, GB300 and RTX PRO Server records often store normalized tera rates in reported. Preserve source PFLOPS/POPS, column, sparse/dense convention and conversion formula.

F03.title: A100 primary peak table describes 40GB SXM4, not both selected 80GB SKUs
F03.detail: A100 whitepaper Table 4 explicitly has SXM4/40GB. The archived A100 product page corroborates 80GB rates, but must be attached to each peak as SKU evidence. Accumulator architecture evidence remains distinct from SKU throughput; do not copy 1410MHz to PCIe/80GB without matching evidence.

F04.title: B200/B300 power exists in a different archived profile
F04.detail: Blackwell brief Table 3 printed p26 gives per-GPU maximum TDP 1000W B200, 1100W B300. Current notes explicitly segregate its memory/bandwidth profile. Add candidate evidence, keep power null until profile compatibility is resolved; no silent cross-revision merge.

F05.title: Non-Tensor label is not an explicit accumulator statement
F05.detail: Vector input/rate rows establish non-Tensor performance. Matching accumulator precision is not explicitly stated by these tables. Keep a separate instruction-level proof obligation rather than treating a source pointer as proof.

F06.title: Architecture instruction typing does not alone bind SKU advertised peak
F06.detail: PTX establishes allowed BF16/TF32/INT8 combinations. A SKU peak also requires documented mapping to that instruction family and rate. Existing supporting claims are useful, but mechanical eligibility is not content acceptance.

F07.title: Clock and power association incomplete
F07.detail: Most peak clock_basis strings contain no frequency or peak-specific source. TDP/TGP caps are not operating power at the published rate. H100 Table 3 clock rows omit explicit INT8 and FP16/BF16 non-Tensor labels; do not expand the listed clock domains by analogy.

F08.title: H200 source mislabels INT8 rate as TFLOPS
F08.detail: H200 datasheet INT8 row literally says TFLOPS. Catalog operation_kind=integer is correct; record the source unit typo and TOPS normalization explicitly, as already done for Atlas350.

F09.title: Known unknowns remain unresolved and nonselectable
F09.detail: Unspecified precision/accumulator/unit/sparsity must remain unspecified. Empty peak arrays do not prove non-support or official nondisclosure across all publications.

F10.title: Source-lock archive note contains unrelated CloudMatrix text
F10.detail: nvidia-blackwell-brief archive_note refers to CloudMatrix author paper; this is incorrect metadata for an NVIDIA technical brief.

F11.title: Unit conversions and revision differences do not authorize new peaks
F11.detail: Keep GB300 FP4 1080/1440 PFLOPS and INT8 12/24 POPS as published; no forced doubling or substitution from GB200. Keep Ascend950 combined rounded totals as published. Preserve Rubin training/inference and GPU-column scope.
